# phase-093 — Stop rebuilding from cold on every push, and run the fast tier first  [MANUAL — bot has no workflows scope]

## You must change `.github/workflows/`

This phase declares `must_touch: [.github/workflows/]`. The gate fails the phase unless at
least one changed file falls under it. Writing tests, documentation or a report
is not enough — if you finish without touching that area, the phase fails on
exactly that check.


## Evidence — verified finding

```
Every push pays a cold build and every push runs the whole corpus. .github/workflows/ci.yml triggers on both push and pull_request to main, and its only job begins at `cargo build` with no cache step, so target/ is discarded between runs. The suite has a natural fast tier and a slow tier that are not separated: unit tests, the linter, the formatter and the LSP finish in seconds, while the 722-file corpus differential harness dominates the wall clock. Paying the full cost to learn that a line is misformatted is waste that repeats on every push. NOTE: this phase changes .github/workflows/, and the rbops bot token deliberately has NO `workflows` permission (.github/workflows/rbops.yml:10) so that an agent cannot edit its own gate. An agent CANNOT land this phase. It is declared manual and is applied by a human push.
```

**Re-verify this before you change anything.** If the finding no longer
reproduces on `main`, stop and write that to `FINDINGS.md` — a stale phase must
never be "fixed" by inventing a change.

## Goal

Cache target/ between runs keyed on the lockfile hash. Split the workflow so a fast job runs fmt, clippy, the unit/linter/formatter/LSP tests and the README blocks, and the sharded full suite runs only where it is needed - on merge to main and on pull requests, not on every push to a branch that has no pull request. A push that only opens the fast tier should finish in minutes. Keep every check that can catch a bad commit in the fast tier, so nothing is lost by not running the slow tier on branch pushes. MANUAL: the agent that dispatches this must not attempt it; the change is pushed by a human with workflow scope.

## Method

1. Read `AGENTS.md` in full. Obey every hard rule; they are not negotiable.
2. Reproduce the finding. Record the exact command and the exact wrong output.
3. Write the failing test FIRST. Watch it fail. Do not touch production code
   until you have a red test that fails for the right reason.
4. Make the smallest change that turns it green.
5. Run the four gates yourself before claiming anything:

   ```bash
   cargo fmt --all -- --check
   cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings
   cargo test --all-targets
   ./rbops/verify.sh phase-093
   ```

6. Write `REPORT.md` in the exact shape required by `AGENTS.md` section 4.

## Definition of done

- [ ] this phase is applied by a human push, not by the bot - an agent attempting it will have its push refused, which is the intended lock
- [ ] target/ is cached between runs and a second push does not recompile the workspace from scratch - proven by CI logs, not asserted
- [ ] a push to a branch with no pull request runs the fast tier and does not run the corpus differential job
- [ ] the fast tier still catches a formatting error, proven by a deliberate bad-format push in a test run recorded in REPORT.md
- [ ] the full suite still runs on pull_request and on push to main
- [ ] the fast tier's wall clock is recorded in REPORT.md and is a small fraction of the full suite's
- [ ] no check present before this phase is now unreachable on any trigger - each is listed in REPORT.md with the trigger that runs it

## Constraints

- Do not touch `.github/workflows/`, `rbops/`, `.opencode/agent/`, or

## If you are blocked

Do not fake progress. Write what you tried, the exact error, and what you
believe is required into `FINDINGS.md`, then stop.

A blocked phase with an honest report is worth more than a green phase with a
lie in it. `verify.sh` will reject the phase anyway; a fabrication only adds a
blocking review finding on top.
